sections: White to yellowish-white crystalline or amorphous powder.
Not applicable – mixture of cysteine proteases from Ananas comosus (EC 3.4.22.32 stem bromelain)
Yellow crystalline powder; melting point 242 °C; water solubility 12.5 mg/100 mL.

Trypsin: Named in 1876 by German physiologist Wilhelm Kühne (from Greek 'thrýpto' – 'I break'); obtained from bovine or porcine pancreas. First approval/introduction: Pharmaceutical use of pancreatic proteases since the mid-20th century. Bromelain: Extracted commercially from pineapple stems (Thailand, Malaysia); heat-labile (≈83% activity remains after 1 h at 50 °C). First approval/introduction: EMA 2012: bromelain-based topical product approved for debridement of severe burns. Rutoside Trihydrate (Rutin): Found in buckwheat, citrus, Ruta graveolens and asparagus; under research for venous insufficiency and post-thrombotic syndrome. First approval/introduction: Used as a vasoprotective in Europe since the mid-20th century.
Trypsin 96 mg + Bromelain 180 mg + Rutoside trihydrate 200 mg

Trypsin and bromelain are proteolytic enzymes that degrade inflammatory debris and fibrin, reducing oedema; rutoside protects capillaries and reduces permeability – synergistic anti-oedematous action.

Trypsin Serine protease that hydrolyses proteins in inflammatory exudate and fibrin deposits, reducing oedema and accelerating resolution of inflammation and haematoma. Receptor / target profile: Cleaves peptide bonds on the carboxyl side of lysine and arginine; degrades fibrin and inflammatory debris.

Bromelain Cysteine protease mixture that modulates inflammatory mediators (bradykinin, prostaglandins), reduces oedema, has fibrinolytic and anti-platelet effects. Receptor / target profile: Sulfhydryl proteases that modulate bradykinin and prostaglandin pathways, reduce oedema, and have fibrinolytic and antiplatelet effects.

Reduces capillary permeability and fragility, scavenges free radicals and inhibits inflammatory mediators, complementing proteolytic enzymes in reducing oedema. Receptor / target profile: Reduces capillary permeability and fragility; antioxidant; inhibits platelet aggregation and inflammatory mediators.
Small fraction absorbed intact; binds alpha-1-antitrypsin and alpha-2-macroglobulin
Summary: Enteric-coated; a fraction is absorbed intact from the intestine and bound to alpha-2-macroglobulin.
Partially absorbed intact (~40% reported in animal studies)
Summary: Partially absorbed intact from the gut.

Colonic deglycosylation to quercetin; hepatic conjugation
Summary: Partly absorbed; hydrolysed by gut flora to quercetin.
Post-traumatic and post-operative oedema and inflammation
Sprains, contusions, fractures with soft-tissue swelling
Two tablets three times daily for the first 2–3 days, then 1 tablet three times daily (or as directed)
Take at least 30 minutes before or 1 hour after meals with water; swallow whole
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
May increase absorption of some antibiotics (amoxicillin, tetracycline)
Bromelain: Take on an empty stomach.
Rutoside Trihydrate (Rutin): With or without food.
Trypsin: Supportive care. Bromelain: Supportive care. Rutoside Trihydrate (Rutin): Supportive care.
Klein & Kullich, 2000; Akhtar et al., 2004 – oral enzyme–rutoside combination comparable to diclofenac in knee osteoarthritis.
Studies in post-traumatic oedema show faster reduction of swelling.
Inform if allergic to pineapple, papaya or latex
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
